New concept 'moderate_severe_immunocompromise' was used for the age-18 exclusion. The vocabulary's 'immunocompromised' (any immunocompromising condition) is broader than 'moderately or severely immunocompromised', so it was not forced.

Limitation of COVID-VAX-18: the numerator counts any single COVID-19 vaccine dose. Unvaccinated persons receiving Novavax need 2 doses ('2 doses 2024–25 Novavax at 0, 3–8 weeks'). The covid19_vaccine concept does not distinguish products, so a single Novavax dose in an unvaccinated person would be wrongly counted as complete.

Limitation of COVID-VAX-18: the measurement-year window cannot exactly represent a named seasonal formulation ('2024–25'). The window is derived and the rule will need updating when the formulation changes.
Not represented for age 18 (previously vaccinated): the minimum interval of at least 8 weeks after the most recent dose.
Not represented for age 18 (prior single Novavax dose): the 3–8 week Novavax follow-up interval, and the alternative product choice if more than 8 weeks have passed.

COVID-19 vaccination for ages 6 months–17 years who are not moderately or severely immunocompromised is shared clinical decision-making. It depends on clinician judgment, parent preference and circumstances, so it is not encoded as a rule.

The 6 months–17 years section also contains product- and history-dependent dose schedules that were not encoded: Moderna 2 doses vs Pfizer-BioNTech 3 doses for unvaccinated children 6 months–4 years, completion of incomplete initial series, and same-manufacturer requirements.
Not represented: minimum ages by product (6 months for Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech; 12 years for Novavax).
Not represented: recommendations for moderately or severely immunocompromised persons, which are not given in this section.
Persons aged 19 years or older are referred to the Adult Immunization Schedule, 2025, and are not covered here.

The general 'Additional information' items are dose-validity and administrative guidance, not representable as rules: interval calculation (4 weeks = 28 days), the 4-day grace period and invalid-dose repeat logic, travel vaccination, immunodeficiency tables, outbreak guidance, and VICP/CICP compensation.
